correctness.rationale: Rebuilt the proof from the actual signed clique inequalities for K=unconditional stable-set polytope of a perfect graph. For an arbitrary positive definite Q with E_Q inside K, averaging signed clique support inequalities gives diagonal s=(q_ii) in P_G. By the stable-set convex decomposition, the theta-weighted average of sum_{i in T}1/s_i is exactly d, so some stable T attains >=d. For every signed 1_T in K, outer ellipsoid inclusion and sign averaging give lambda^2>=sum_{i in T}(Q^{-1})_ii>=sum1/s_i>=d via the Cauchy-Schwarz diagonal inverse inequality. Symmetric John gives lambda<=sqrt(d), including d=1. Independently checked the signed-clique reciprocal certificates with exact fractions for sample three- and four-vertex graphs and non-diagonal positive definite test matrices; the all-d proof is analytic and does not rely on finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Unconditional reflexive lattice polytopes only; not arbitrary unconditional convex bodies or non-reflexive stable-set constructions.

originality.rationale: Kohl–Olsen–Sanyal full paper classifies the objects as perfect-graph signed stable-set polytopes but does not evaluate their Euclidean Banach–Mazur distances. Grundbacher–Kobos full current equality-case paper proves the universal bound and low-dimensional classification, not that every unconditional reflexive graph polytope is a maximizer in all d. Exact database searches found only other polytope radii/John shape, which do not imply an optimum over all ellipsoids. Best-of-knowledge class-wide assertion survives.
